links.claim: See XLS-85 and xrpl.js flag 17. No mainnet support is claimed. - The writer receives the principal only by publishing K through a successful finish. A relay can submit the same fulfillment; funds still go to the original destination. Buyer cancellation is policy-only and cannot win before expiry. - K becomes public. This is acceptable because each ciphertext is encrypted for one buyer and intent with a fresh key; it does not unlock other buyers' copies. It is not DRM: anyone with that ciphertext and public K can read that copy. - A writer can commit to nonsense or an undecryptable envelope and collect. The cryptographic proof establishes responsibility, not truth or automatic damages. Existing challenges/reputation handle broken promises; this is not a truth oracle. - K may appear in an unvalidated submitted finish. The buyer still waits for validation. Ledger outages/history gaps retain reservations pending reconciliation. - A dishonest buyer can create extra escrow objects outside policy. This product guarantees one charge per policy intent, not control of arbitrary wallet activity. - Conditional finish costs more than a Payment. The XRPL fee formula scales as base_fee × (33 + fulfillment_bytes / 16) before multisign/load effects. Here K is 32 bytes and its encoded fulfillment is 36 bytes. At the observed 12-drop signing base, ceil(12 × (33 + 36/16)) = 423 drops. A 2,000-drop cap rejects excessive fees. Live create/cancel each cost 12 drops. A cancelled 60,000-drop principal is fully returned; its buyer still pays 24 drops in fees. - Synthetic corpus and extractive fixture answers in the proof are labelled; Testnet value transfer is real Testnet execution, with no real value.

links.claim: RLUSD escrow support cannot be inferred from an XRP key-reveal purchase. The team documented official RLUSD as blocked until its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking. Our alternative is TEST-SGD, an IOU issued by our own Testnet issuer with no real value. It stands in for RLUSD in a mechanism experiment; it is neither official RLUSD nor evidence of stablecoin adoption. The docs contain no verified list of Singapore banks piloting RLUSD settlement in 2026. We cannot name banks from this evidence.

links.claim: The issuer is separate from buyer and writer. Policy rejects issuer-as-party, missing permission, nonzero transfer fees, frozen/unauthorized lines, insufficient balance or destination limit before create signing. This is a conservative subset of XLS-85: no transfer-fee arithmetic or freeze exception is claimed. Settlement checks the writer RippleState balance delta (currency, issuer, sign and exact value), never the requested Amount as proof of delivery. Cancellation checks the buyer's returned balance delta. Existing reservations and signed outboxes remain.
